title: Novel biomarkers for contrast-induced acute kidney injury identified from RNA sequencing data
description: Contrast-induced acute kidney injury (CI-AKI) is a serious complication of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Emerging evidence suggests that messengerRNAs (mRNAs) and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) could serve as biomarkers for various diseases. Overall design: 4 patients with postoperative CI-AKI (case group) and 4 patients without CI-AKI (control group) were enrolled among the patients hospitalized in our department undergoing elective PCI. The groups were matched in terms of age, sex, and comorbidities (diabetes, heart failure).

samples.title: 15 - Control
attributes: The 56-year-old male did not develop contrast-induced acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after the elective PCI procedure. He belongs to the control group. His baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 42.582 ml/min. He has hypertension and diabetes but does not have atrial fibrillation or heart failure.
